definition: A single line of rap lyrics. In music, a bar is a measure of time — rappers use it to mean one line or one unit of their verse.
origin: Musical term adopted by hip-hop. DJs and producers count in bars; rappers write in them.
example_lines: Spit 16 bars and the crowd goes crazy
That bar right there was cold

definition: A verse of 16 bars — the standard length for a rap verse on a song. When someone says 'drop a 16,' they mean rap a full verse.
origin: Standard song structure. Verses in hip-hop are typically 16 bars.
example_lines: I need you to drop a 16 on this beat

definition: The payoff line in a rap — the funny, clever, or devastating line that closes a setup. A great punchline rewards the listener for paying attention.
origin: Comedy term brought into hip-hop. a pioneering MC is widely credited with elevating punchlines to an art form.
example_lines: That punchline was so hard I had to rewind it

definition: A song made specifically to insult and attack another artist — exposing their weaknesses, lies, or past actions. The most serious form of rap beef.
origin: Short for 'disrespect track.' A cornerstone of hip-hop culture since the Roxanne Wars in the 1980s.
example_lines: He dropped a diss track and it was over for shorty

definition: A serious dispute or conflict between rappers, crews, or labels. Can be verbal (through music) or escalate to real confrontation.
origin: Slang for argument or grievance. Became central to hip-hop via East Coast/West Coast rivalry of the 90s.
example_lines: The beef between them two goes way back
That's old beef — dead that

definition: A shot taken at someone without naming them directly — could be a metaphor, a shade, or a reference that only the target and insiders will recognize.
origin: Rap beef tactic. Allows artists to attack without being directly called out, maintaining plausible deniability.
example_lines: That was a subliminal — he didn't say no name but everybody knew

definition: The rhythm, cadence, and timing of how a rapper delivers their words over a beat. A good flow fits the music naturally and feels effortless.
origin: Core element of rap technique. Often what separates good rappers from elite ones.
example_lines: His flow on that track is crazy
She switched her flow three times in one verse

definition: Rhyming multiple syllables instead of just the last word. The most technically demanding form of rap lyricism — used by a Bronx MC, a Detroit rapper, and others at the elite level.
origin: a pioneering MC pioneered this in the late 80s. Big L, a Bronx MC, and a Detroit rapper took it to extremes.
example_lines: His multisyllabic rhyme scheme is unmatched

definition: The chorus — the most memorable, repeated part of a song. The hook is designed to stick in your head and carry the song's main message.
origin: Music production term. In hip-hop, hooks are often sung or semi-sung by the rapper or a featured vocalist.
example_lines: That hook is infectious — it's been stuck in my head all week

definition: The spontaneous-sounding phrases or words a rapper says in the background while the main vocals play — 'yeah,' 'uh,' 'let's go,' etc. Often become a rapper's signature.
origin: From Latin 'ad libitum' meaning at one's pleasure. In hip-hop, ad libs are a signature element — think a luxury fashion brand's 'Burrr' or a Philadelphia rapper's screams.
example_lines: His ad libs go harder than most rappers' verses

definition: Style, fashion, or the way someone carries themselves aesthetically. High drip = looking extremely good. Can also refer to jewelry.
origin: Atlanta, early 2010s. Popularized by an Atlanta rapper and the ATL trap scene.
example_lines: The drip is immaculate
He came through with the drip on a thousand

definition: Style, charisma, confidence — the intangible quality that makes someone cool. Similar to drip but more about personality than clothing.
origin: Atlanta/Southern rap. Popularized by an Atlanta rapper and Young Dolph.
example_lines: Can't teach the sauce, you either got it or you don't

definition: A thousand dollars. 'Racks' typically means multiple thousands. 'A rack' = $1,000. 'Ten racks' = $10,000.
origin: Originated in the South. 'Rack' from the slang for $1,000 bundles of cash.
example_lines: Spent racks on the fit
She need racks just to talk to me

definition: Same as racks — thousands of dollars. A 'band' is $1,000 because bills are banded together in $1,000 bundles at the bank.
origin: Southern rap, popularized in the 2010s.
example_lines: He's pulling bands like it's nothing

definition: 1. A trap house — a location where drugs are sold. 2. A genre of rap music that originated in Atlanta characterized by hi-hat rolls, 808 drums, and dark subject matter about street life.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. an Atlanta rapper popularized the term with 'Trap Muzik' (2003). an Atlanta rapper and Young an Atlanta rapper built the sound.
example_lines: Started from the trap, now I'm on top
That's a certified trap banger

definition: The source — the connect. Someone who provides drugs, exclusive goods, or access to things others can't get. 'The plug' is the supplier.
origin: Street term adopted across hip-hop. 'Plug' as in plugging someone in — connecting them to what they need.
example_lines: I'm the plug, they come to me
He hit the plug for a re-up

definition: Diamond jewelry. Specifically refers to diamonds set in chains, rings, watches, and grills. The 'ice' is the sparkle and shine of the diamonds.
origin: New York, late 90s. Popularized by Raekwon ('Iced Out'), then exploded with the bling era (Birdman, a New Orleans rapper).
example_lines: The ice on his wrist got the club lit
She dripping in ice from head to toe

definition: VVS stands for 'Very Very Slightly Included' — a diamond clarity grade just below flawless. In rap, VVS = the highest-quality diamonds you can get.
origin: Jewelry industry terminology adopted by hip-hop. 2 Chainz and an Atlanta rap group helped bring it into mainstream use.
example_lines: VVS diamonds, no inclusions
That chain got VVS stones all through it

definition: Original Gangster — someone who has been in the game from the beginning, earned their respect, and carries authority. OGs are veterans who command deference.
origin: LA gang culture, early 80s. Ice-T popularized it in rap with 'O.G. Original Gangster' (1991).
example_lines: He's an OG, you better show respect
The OGs don't mess with the new generation

definition: Someone who writes raps for an artist who then performs them as their own — without credit. One of the most serious accusations you can make in hip-hop.
origin: Common in the music industry. In hip-hop, it's considered a major violation because authenticity and 'writing your own rhymes' is a core value.
example_lines: They say he uses a ghostwriter — that finished his credibility
a Philadelphia rapper exposed his ghostwriter

definition: A guest verse on someone else's song. Artists 'feature' on tracks for a fee, as a favor, or to build relationships. Also called a 'collab.'
origin: Standard practice across music. In hip-hop features became a major business starting in the 90s.
example_lines: That feature he dropped was better than the main artist's verse

definition: Writing ability — the skill of crafting lyrics. 'Strong pen game' means someone writes exceptional bars. The pen is mightier than the rapper who can't write.
origin: Hip-hop term for writing craft. 'The pen' represents the actual writing of lyrics.
example_lines: His pen game is elite — every line hits different

definition: A circle of rappers who take turns freestyling or spitting verses — usually unplanned, raw, and competitive. Ciphers test your skills without studio production.
origin: From '5 Percenter' Nation of Gods and Earths culture, adopted into hip-hop. a hip-hop TV network Hip Hop Awards made ciphers famous to mainstream audiences.
example_lines: He bodied that cipher — nobody could touch him

definition: The Roland TR-808 — a drum machine from 1980 whose bass drum sound became the foundation of hip-hop, trap, and R&B. When you feel that deep, rumbling bass kick, that's the 808.
origin: Roland Corporation, 1980. a founding figure of hip-hop used it on 'Planet Rock.' It defines modern trap music.
example_lines: That 808 knocked the whole block
a Chicago producer-rapper's 808s & Heartbreak changed music forever

definition: Taking a portion of an existing song — usually a melody, drum pattern, or vocal line — and incorporating it into a new track. Sampling is foundational to hip-hop.
origin: Hip-hop's core production technique since the Bronx block parties. DJ a founding DJ of hip-hop invented looping breakbeats.
example_lines: They sampled James Brown — can't go wrong with that
The whole beat is built around that soul sample

definition: Rapping off the top of your head — improvised, unwritten lyrics delivered in real time. True freestyles are a sign of mental quickness and lyrical skill.
origin: Core hip-hop tradition. In the 80s-90s, freestyle battles in New York parks and radio shows determined reputations.
example_lines: He did a 10-minute freestyle off the dome — no notes

definition: To completely destroy someone in a rap battle, verse, or performance. To 'body' a track means to rap so hard that you kill it. If you got bodied, you lost badly.
origin: Battle rap slang. Metaphor: you 'murdered' the track or your opponent so hard they're a body.
example_lines: a West Coast MC bodied that verse
He bodied everyone in that cipher

definition: A phrase with two meanings — one obvious, one hidden. The hidden meaning is usually more clever, dark, or explicit. One of the highest-value tools in a rapper's lyrical arsenal.
origin: French term for 'double meaning.' a pioneering New York rapper, a New Orleans rapper, and a West Coast MC are masters of double entendres.
example_lines: That bar was a double entendre — took me a minute to catch it

definition: Someone who gives information to the police or authorities about criminal activity. The absolute worst thing you can be in street culture. 'Snitching' destroys respect.
origin: Street code term. In hip-hop, the 'no snitching' code is central to authenticity.
example_lines: He got labeled a snitch — career over

definition: Social power, influence, and fame — especially online. Having clout means people pay attention to you, follow you, and care what you say.
origin: Old English word for influence/power. Revived and redefined by social media culture in the 2010s.
example_lines: He's chasing clout instead of real respect
All that clout and can't fill a room

definition: A term associated with Brooklyn rap crew linked to a Brooklyn drill rapper and the Woo gang. Also used as a general exclamation in NYC drill.
origin: Brooklyn, New York. Popularized by a Brooklyn drill rapper and his Brooklyn drill crew in 2019-2020.
example_lines: Woo! Brooklyn in the building

definition: To smoothly manipulate or trick someone out of their money or possessions — with style. To finesse is to pull off a con so smoothly it looks like skill.
origin: French word for skill/subtlety. In hip-hop it took on the meaning of a smooth hustle.
example_lines: He finessed his way into VIP
She finessed that whole situation

definition: Exciting, electric, or in an amazing state. A 'lit' party is wild and fun. A 'lit' bar is fire. Describes high energy, positive chaos.
origin: AAVE slang going back decades. Reached mainstream usage around 2015-2016 via social media.
example_lines: The section was lit from start to finish

definition: Greatest Of All Time. The ultimate compliment in hip-hop — declaring someone the undisputed best ever. a Brooklyn MC, a West Coast MC, a pioneering New York rapper, a Detroit rapper, a Queensbridge MC, a West Coast MC all have GOAT claims.
origin: Sports term (especially boxing/Muhammad Ali) adopted by hip-hop. a New York rapper popularized it in rap.
example_lines: He's the GOAT — no debate
The GOAT debate in hip-hop never ends

definition: Restocking supply — originally drugs, but used broadly for getting more of anything you need. Can also mean re-signing a deal or renewing a contract.
origin: Drug trade terminology adopted into hip-hop vocabulary.
example_lines: Had to hit the plug for a re-up
Time to re-up the contract

definition: When a song sounds incredible, especially on a good sound system. A track that 'slaps' hits hard and makes people react.
origin: West Coast slang going back to the 90s — about how bass-heavy music feels when it hits.
example_lines: That new joint slaps in the whip
Turn this up — it slaps

definition: Not lying — this is the truth. 'Cap' means a lie. 'No cap' means no lie, I'm being completely serious.
origin: AAVE slang. Atlanta origins. 'Cap' as slang for lie goes back decades but 'no cap' exploded around 2017-2018.
example_lines: That was the hardest verse of the year, no cap

definition: A lie. 'That's cap' = that's a lie. When someone is 'capping,' they're being dishonest or exaggerating.
origin: AAVE slang. The opposite of 'no cap.'
example_lines: That's cap — he wasn't even there
Stop capping on the internet

definition: Immediate confrontation — the moment you see someone, there's going to be conflict. 'It's on sight' means no conversation, just action.
origin: Street culture term. Means no need for provocation once you see the person.
example_lines: Since the diss dropped, it's on sight
They beef so hard it's on sight every time they cross paths

definition: A fight — or specifically, a one-on-one fight. 'Get a fade' means fight me. Also refers to a type of haircut (short on the sides, longer on top).
origin: Dual meaning. As a fight term, it's Southern/universal street slang. As a haircut, it's a classic barbershop term.
example_lines: He caught a fade behind that
Pull up and get this fade

definition: Completely serious, no joke. New York intensifier meaning 'I am dead serious right now.' Can be used as a question ('deadass?') or a statement.
origin: Brooklyn and the Bronx. Core AAVE/NYC slang that spread nationally through social media.
example_lines: Deadass that verse went crazy, no debate

definition: Agreement, affirmation, or acknowledgment — the NYC equivalent of 'facts.' Can mean 'I agree,' 'is that right?' or 'say less.' One word carrying infinite meaning.
origin: New York City hip-hop since the 1980s. Foundational NYC slang.
example_lines: Word, that album is a classic — no argument

definition: A term of address in New York hip-hop — calling someone 'son' signals familiarity and brotherhood. Rooted in 5 Percenter theology where 'son' and 'sun' are interchangeable.
origin: New York City, rooted in 5 Percenter Nation of Gods and Earths culture. Heavy in Bronx, Harlem, and Brooklyn since the 80s.
example_lines: Son came through with that verse and shut the whole cipher down

definition: A New York term of address, short for 'brother' — used the same way as 'son' or 'kid.' Classic NYC shorthand for addressing someone you know.
origin: New York City street slang. Used heavily in Brooklyn and Bronx hip-hop culture since the 80s.
example_lines: Nah B, that beat was mid — don't play me like that

definition: Exceptionally skilled, raw, or impressive. In NYC hip-hop, 'ill' is one of the highest compliments — dangerously talented. a pioneering MC built a legacy around being 'ill.'
origin: New York City hip-hop, 1980s. Core golden era NYC vocabulary.
example_lines: That beat selection was ill — can't even front

definition: Definitely excellent — top tier. 'Def' in NYC golden era hip-hop meant undeniably good. It's where a major hip-hop label Records got its name.
origin: New York City hip-hop, early 1980s. Rick Rubin and Russell Simmons named their label 'a major hip-hop label' in 1984.
example_lines: That album was def — every track certified

definition: Outstanding, excellent, impressive. One of hip-hop's most universal adjectives. Also literally refers to drugs, creating a classic double meaning.
origin: New York City, 1980s. AAVE term repurposed by hip-hop culture.
example_lines: That's a dope beat — who produced it?

definition: Clean, stylish, and put-together. A 'fresh' outfit is crisp and on point. a New York rapper built an entire identity around being fresh.
origin: New York City, early 1980s hip-hop. a foundational New York rap group's a major sportswear brand culture. Fresh is foundational NYC flex vocabulary.
example_lines: Came through fresh to death — no wrinkles, no creases

definition: Raw, unpolished, and rooted in the streets — not pretty but authentic. A 'grimey' track has grit and edge. A 'grimey' person is conniving and not to be trusted.
origin: New York City, especially East New York and South Bronx. 90s underground rap scene. Mobb Deep made grimey an aesthetic.
example_lines: That beat is grimey — sounds like a rooftop in the BX at 3am

definition: Acting reckless, out of control, or excessively — either positively (going crazy at the party) or negatively (behaving dangerously). 'Wildin out' is the full phrase.
origin: New York City AAVE. Used heavily in 90s and 2000s NYC hip-hop.
example_lines: He was wildin on that verse — said everything

definition: Overdoing it — way too much. In NYC slang 'OD' means excessively or to an extreme degree. Can be positive ('that drip is OD') or negative.
origin: New York City. Literally from 'overdose' but used figuratively. Core NYC slang.
example_lines: The jewelry is OD — blinding everybody in the room

definition: Two meanings: 1. Extremely cold — 'it's brick outside' (NYC). 2. A kilogram of cocaine compressed into a brick shape — a major drug unit.
origin: NYC cold weather slang and drug trade terminology. Both usages established in hip-hop.
example_lines: It's brick out here, son — we moving in furs
He moved a brick every week from the bando

definition: The most versatile word in Philly slang — it can mean literally anything. A person, a place, a thing, a situation. 'That jawn right there' could refer to a car, a song, or a moment.
origin: Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. A Philly-specific term linguists have actually studied.
example_lines: You heard that new jawn he dropped? That jawn is crazy

definition: A Dutch Masters cigarillo used to roll blunts. 'Rolling a dutch' means emptying the tobacco and filling with weed.
origin: Dutch Masters brand cigars. Northeast rap culture. New York and Philadelphia especially.
example_lines: Sparked a dutch and let the session run

definition: Pretending to be something you're not — faking wealth, toughness, or status. If you're frontin, you're putting on a show that doesn't match reality.
origin: New York City hip-hop. Pharrell and a pioneering New York rapper had a song called 'Frontin' in 2003 that cemented the term nationally.
example_lines: He's frontin on the internet but can't afford the rent

definition: A Southern term for a woman or girl, used affectionately. Also used in Atlanta to mean a young man or friend. Context determines gender.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. Southern rap slang that became nationally used. an Atlanta producer-rapper, Ludacris, and an Atlanta rap duo helped spread it in the 2000s.
example_lines: Shawty bad — she pulled up looking immaculate

definition: A close friend, a genuine associate — someone you really trust. 'Slime' signals deep loyalty. an Atlanta rapper made it his signature term and it became essential Atlanta vocabulary.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. Popularized by an Atlanta rapper and YSL (Young Stoner Life). Spread nationally through trap music.
example_lines: That's my slime — ride or die since the sandbox

definition: Extreme heat or intensity — either from law enforcement, enemies, or the weight of the streets. Also used to describe someone whose music or presence is overwhelming.
origin: Atlanta trap culture, popularized by an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper in the 2010s.
example_lines: He's putting pressure on everybody — can't nobody match him right now

definition: A lick or a come-up — stealing, robbing, or scamming someone successfully. 'Hit a jugg' means you pulled off a heist or theft.
origin: Atlanta slang for robbery or theft. Used across Southern trap rap in the 2010s.
example_lines: Hit a jugg and came back with the whole re-up money

definition: A robbery or theft — hitting a 'lick' means successfully robbing someone or a place.
origin: Street slang with roots in Southern hip-hop culture.
example_lines: Hit a lick at the corner store and fed the whole crew

definition: A large amount of money — not specific to a denomination, just a lot of cash. 'Getting guap' means making serious money.
origin: New York City slang that spread nationally. Popularized in the early 2000s.
example_lines: Counted up the guap and bought the block

definition: An abandoned house or building used to sell drugs. The trap house of trap houses — where you cook and serve product out of a vacant property.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. Trap culture term.
example_lines: Started serving out the bando before we had a studio
Came from the bando to the penthouse — that's the story

definition: A supply of drugs for distribution. 'Moving a pack' means selling drugs. 'The pack came through' means the supply arrived.
origin: Drug trade terminology used across all trap rap — Atlanta, Chicago, Houston, and beyond.
example_lines: Pack hit at midnight, by sunrise it was gone

definition: Enemies — opponents or opposition. Your 'opps' are people who are against you, beef with you, or have violated your crew. Chicago drill made this term essential.
origin: Chicago, Illinois. Drill music culture. Popularized by Chief Keef and the GBE crew around 2012. Short for 'opponents.'
example_lines: Can't slide through that block — the opps are everywhere

definition: To go to where your enemies are to confront or attack them. 'Sliding on' someone means going to their location with hostile intent.
origin: Chicago drill culture. Associated with Chief Keef, G Herbo, and the Chicago scene of the 2010s.
example_lines: They disrespected so we slid on them that same night

definition: To drive through enemy territory multiple times — going around the block repeatedly to find opps. A particularly aggressive form of retaliation.
origin: Chicago drill. Popularized in the 2010s through Chief Keef and G Herbo's music about street retaliation.
example_lines: They came through once — we spun the block three times

definition: A nickname for Chicago — combining 'Chicago' and 'Iraq' to highlight the city's historically high murder rate and constant gang warfare.
origin: Chicago, Illinois. Coined in the early 2010s. Director Spike Lee made a film titled 'Chi-Raq' (2015).
example_lines: Straight from Chiraq where survival is the daily mission

definition: Someone who actively goes to war — who steps to enemies without hesitation. A steppa is not a talker, they act.
origin: Chicago drill and UK drill culture.
example_lines: He ain't just a rapper — he's a real steppa

definition: A Chicago oath sworn on a deceased or incarcerated friend — the highest form of emphasis in Chicago street culture.
origin: Chicago, Illinois. Deeply embedded in Chicago street and drill culture.
example_lines: On bro that verse was the hardest one all year

definition: A custom, old-school American car — usually a Cadillac or Buick — decked out with candy paint, swangas (wire wheels), and a booming sound system. The ultimate Houston status symbol. SLAB = Slow, Low, and Bangin.
origin: Houston, Texas. A cornerstone of Houston car culture and rap aesthetics.
example_lines: Pulled up in the slab, candy red, swangas scraping

definition: Large, protruding wire spoke rims — also called 'elbows' — that extend past the wheel well of a car. A defining feature of Houston slab culture.
origin: Houston, Texas. The large 83-spoke wire wheels became iconic in the early 2000s.
example_lines: Whipping the Caddy on swangas, candy paint dripping

definition: A music production technique from Houston — slowing down a song and adding skips, stutters, and repeats to create a woozy, hypnotic sound. DJ Screw invented it.
origin: Houston, Texas. Created by DJ Screw (Robert Earl Davis Jr.) in the early 1990s.
example_lines: The chopped and screwed version hits different at midnight

definition: A recreational drug cocktail made from prescription promethazine/codeine cough syrup mixed with soda (usually Sprite). Highly addictive, deeply embedded in Houston rap culture.
origin: Houston, Texas. Known as 'purple drank,' 'syrup,' or 'sizzurp.' DJ Screw and a Memphis rap group popularized it.
example_lines: Double cup full of lean, moving slow through the night

definition: Lean mixed with Sprite — Sprite being the soda of choice for mixing codeine syrup. an Atlanta rapper's 'a slang name for lean' mixtape made this a landmark phrase in trap music.
origin: Houston/Atlanta crossover. an Atlanta rapper made 'a slang name for lean' iconic in Atlanta trap.
example_lines: a slang name for lean in the double cup — an Atlanta rapper playing in the background

definition: A Bay Area movement characterized by going crazy, losing control, and going dumb on the dance floor. To get 'hyphy' is to go wild, reckless, and free.
origin: Oakland and San Francisco Bay Area, mid-2000s. E-40, Mac Dre, and Keak Da Sneak pioneered the hyphy movement.
example_lines: Bay Area turned up — we getting hyphy in the parking lot

definition: Bay Area slang for 'you know what I mean' — compressed into one rapid phrase. A signature verbal tic of the hyphy era, used constantly by E-40.
origin: Oakland, California. E-40 popularized it.
example_lines: That album was certified classic, yadadamean?

definition: Northern California slang for 'very' or 'a lot of.' 'Hella good' means very good. One of the most distinctly Bay Area words in existence.
origin: San Francisco Bay Area. Used by rappers, skaters, and students alike.
example_lines: That show was hella packed — couldn't even move

definition: Hundred dollar bills — Ben Franklin is on the front and in certain lighting the bills have a blue hue. 'Blue faces' means you have stacks of hundreds.
origin: Trap and Southern rap slang. A visual description of large amounts of cash.
example_lines: Blue faces on the table — we ate good tonight

definition: Large sums of money that require commas when written out — $1,000 and above. 'Counting commas' means making serious money.
origin: National rap slang. References the mathematical notation of large numbers.
example_lines: We ain't talking dollars, we talking commas — that's different

definition: A a luxury fashion house a luxury handbag bag — the most exclusive and expensive handbag in the world, starting around $10,000. In rap, buying someone a a luxury handbag is the ultimate luxury gift.
origin: a luxury fashion house luxury brand. Named after actress Jane a luxury handbag.
example_lines: She got three Birkins before breakfast — that's real love

definition: A watch or piece of jewelry completely covered in diamonds — every surface iced out. Also used as a verb: 'I busted it down' means I put diamonds all over it.
origin: Atlanta and Southern rap. Popularized by an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper.
example_lines: Bust down Rollie — can't even read the time through all these diamonds

definition: Baguette-cut diamonds — rectangular stones set tightly together in rows. Popular in hip-hop for chains, rings, and watch bezels.
origin: Jewelry industry term. Popularized in hip-hop by an Atlanta rap group and New York trap.
example_lines: Baguettes on the bezel, baguettes in the ring — it's a baguette situation

definition: A thick, interlocking chain style — the most classic and recognizable hip-hop chain. Named for its Cuban origins. Comes in gold, white gold, and platinum.
origin: Miami Cuban culture. Adopted by hip-hop in the late 80s and 90s.
example_lines: Cuban link around the neck, 20 karats, no discussion

definition: A car. Any car can be a 'whip,' but the term is used most often for nice vehicles. 'Whipping' means driving.
origin: Comes from the idea of whipping (steering) a vehicle. Used in hip-hop since the 90s.
example_lines: Pulled up in a new whip — everybody looked twice

definition: A foreign luxury car — typically a European brand like a luxury sports car, a luxury sports car, a luxury car, or a luxury car. 'Pushing a foreign' means driving an imported luxury vehicle.
origin: National hip-hop slang. Common in Southern trap and NY rap.
example_lines: Pulled up in a foreign — it's giving European money

definition: a prescription benzodiazepine — a prescription benzodiazepine. Heavily abused in rap culture, especially in mumble rap and an online streaming platform rap eras. Associated with a foggy, detached state.
origin: Pharmaceutical drug. Lil Pump, XXXTentacion, and a Philadelphia rapper Vert made Xan references ubiquitous in the late 2010s.
example_lines: Popped a Xan and let the beat rock me to sleep

definition: an opioid painkiller — a prescription opioid painkiller. Heavily referenced in trap rap. an Atlanta rapper's 'Mask Off' chorus brought it to mainstream awareness.
origin: Pharmaceutical opioid, an opioid painkiller brand name.
example_lines: Percs got me moving slow but the bars still hit

definition: MDMA in powder or crystal form — a euphoria-inducing club drug. Distinct from 'ecstasy' which refers to pressed pills.
origin: Slang for 'molecular' — referencing pure MDMA.
example_lines: Festival season hit different — everybody on molly

definition: Strong-smelling, high-quality marijuana. 'Loud' because the smell is so potent it's impossible to hide — it announces itself.
origin: National hip-hop slang. Refers to the strong odor of premium cannabis strains.
example_lines: He walked in with the loud — whole hallway smelled it

definition: Premium, top-shelf marijuana — so potent it hits you like gasoline. Also used to mean anything of extremely high quality: 'that album is gas.'
origin: National hip-hop and cannabis culture slang. Dual-use term.
example_lines: That pack is straight gas
His verse is gas — nothing but heat

definition: A Backwoods cigar — a rough, natural tobacco leaf cigar used to roll blunts. Became the preferred blunt wrap in hip-hop around the 2010s, replacing dutches and swishers.
origin: Backwoods Smokes brand. Hip-hop and cannabis culture adopted it nationwide.
example_lines: Rolled a backwood fat as a finger before the show

definition: Marijuana rolled inside a cigar wrap — a tobacco leaf exterior filled with weed. Larger and slower burning than a joint. A central element of hip-hop smoke culture.
origin: Originated with Phillies Blunt cigars in New York in the 1980s. Became universal hip-hop culture.
example_lines: Pass the blunt, homie — we in the studio all night

definition: To cook powder cocaine into crack using a stove, baking soda, and water. Also used as a studio metaphor — 'cooking up a hit' in the booth.
origin: Street drug trade terminology. Also adopted as a studio metaphor.
example_lines: Back then we cooked up in the kitchen — now I cook up in the studio

definition: To kill someone. 'Catching a body' means committing a murder. A body count refers to how many people someone has killed.
origin: Street slang used in hip-hop to describe violence. Prominent in Chicago and NYC drill.
example_lines: He caught a body at 17 — the streets took everything

definition: A loyal, fearless enforcer — someone who handles violent situations without hesitation. Having goons means having soldiers ready to act.
origin: General street slang adopted universally in hip-hop.
example_lines: He might be a rapper now but he still got goons on standby

definition: A person who obsessively collects, studies, and acquires rare or limited-edition sneakers. Sneakerhead culture and hip-hop have been inseparable since a foundational New York rap group's 'My a major sportswear brand.'
origin: National culture rooted in New York hip-hop and basketball.
example_lines: He's a real sneakerhead — got every Air Max from 1987 to now

definition: Someone who wears expensive, limited-edition streetwear purely for hype and status — not for personal style. Often dismissive for people who follow trends blindly.
origin: HypeBeast.com website, founded 2005 in Hong Kong.
example_lines: He's a hypebeast — buying everything that drops whether it looks good or not

definition: A sneaker or piece of clothing so rare and desired that it represents the holy grail for collectors. Your 'grail' is the one thing you'd do anything to own.
origin: Sneaker collector culture, adopted from the Holy Grail metaphor.
example_lines: Finally copped the grail — took three years to find a pair in my size

definition: Sneakers or clothing never been worn, still in original packaging. The highest condition grade for collectible footwear.
origin: Sneaker collector culture. 'Dead stock' referred originally to retail inventory that never sold.
example_lines: Deadstock 1985 Air Jordans — worth more than my first car

definition: A rhyme that occurs within a single line — not just at the end — creating a dense, layered sound. Masters like a pioneering MC and a Detroit rapper pack entire lines with internal rhymes.
origin: Poetic technique adopted and elevated by hip-hop. a pioneering MC is considered the pioneer.
example_lines: His internal rhyme scheme is so dense you need a second listen to catch it all

definition: The rhythmic pattern of a rapper's delivery — the rise and fall of syllables, where they hit and where they rest. Great cadence makes lyrics feel inevitable.
origin: Musical and poetic term. In hip-hop, cadence is what distinguishes one rapper's flow from another.
example_lines: His cadence changes three times in one bar — that's mastery

definition: Being 'in the pocket' means your rap is perfectly locked into the rhythm of the beat — not too early, not too late. It feels completely natural and fluid.
origin: Jazz and funk musician term adopted by hip-hop.
example_lines: He was so in the pocket — every syllable landed exactly right

definition: A rap delivery where three syllables are crammed into the space where two would normally go — creating a tumbling, machine-gun effect. an Atlanta rap group popularized it and changed rap forever.
origin: an Atlanta rap group from Atlanta popularized the triplet flow around 2013-2014.
example_lines: He switched to the triplet flow on the bridge and it went crazy

definition: Rapping at twice the normal speed — fitting twice as many syllables into the same musical space. A technical flex showing breath control and lyrical density.
origin: Pioneered by Tech N9ne, Twista, and later a Detroit rapper.
example_lines: He went double time on the last 8 bars — room went silent

definition: A rap style blending singing and rapping — where the delivery is more musical than purely rhythmic. an Atlanta rapper, an Atlanta rapper, and a prominent Toronto-based rapper made melodic rap the dominant style of the 2010s.
origin: Atlanta trap era, 2010s. an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper pioneered emotional, melodic delivery.
example_lines: He switched to melodic rap on the hook and it hit different

definition: To be completely and permanently destroyed in a rap battle or diss. Named after a Queensbridge MC's 2001 diss track 'Ether' — widely considered the greatest diss track ever made, aimed at a pioneering New York rapper.
origin: a Queensbridge MC's 'Ether' (2001). 'Ether' is a chemical that eliminates something. The song was so devastating 'ethered' became a permanent verb.
example_lines: He got ethered on that response track — should've stayed quiet

definition: To be killed or completely destroyed — either literally or in the context of a rap battle. 'Murked' is total annihilation.
origin: Universal street and hip-hop slang used across all regions.
example_lines: He murked that verse — nobody else should've been on the track

definition: To deliver an exceptionally impressive performance — to 'snap' means you went off with energy and quality. When someone snaps, everything clicks perfectly.
origin: Universal hip-hop slang for outstanding performance.
example_lines: She snapped on that verse — carried the whole song

definition: When a reply tweet gets more likes than the original post — indicating widespread disagreement or mockery. 'Getting ratioed' is a public humiliation online.
origin: social media/X culture, late 2010s.
example_lines: He posted that and got ratioed immediately — should've stayed off the timeline

definition: A win — a positive outcome, achievement, or success. Opposite of an L. 'Taking Ws' means consistently succeeding.
origin: Sports slang (W for win) adopted by hip-hop and internet culture in the 2010s.
example_lines: Dropped the album and it debuted at number one — that's a massive W

definition: A loss — a failure, embarrassment, or setback. 'Taking an L' means losing or experiencing a public failure.
origin: Sports slang (L for loss) adopted by hip-hop culture in the 2010s.
example_lines: He took a massive L with that diss — response was way harder

definition: Doing and saying what you want without caring what others think — being completely yourself. Lil B popularized 'based' as a philosophy of radical self-expression.
origin: Lil B 'The BasedGod' from Berkeley, California. 'Based' started as a negative term but Lil B reclaimed it.
example_lines: He gave that interview and didn't care what anyone thought — that's based

definition: Mediocre — average at best, not impressive. Calling something 'mid' means it's neither bad nor good, just unremarkably in the middle.
origin: Internet slang that entered mainstream usage in the early 2020s.
example_lines: The album was mid — nothing skippable but nothing memorable either

definition: When someone lives in your head without you being able to stop thinking about them. 'Living rent free' means occupying mental space without permission.
origin: Internet culture slang, popularized in the 2010s-2020s.
example_lines: He keeps responding — that rapper is living rent free in his head

definition: To be caught unprepared, off-guard, or in a vulnerable position. Originated in street culture where getting caught lacking can mean life or death.
origin: Street culture term popularized through hip-hop.
example_lines: He dropped that diss and the other rapper got caught lacking — no response ready

definition: A transformation — physical, financial, or social — from a lesser state to a superior one. A 'glow up' is the whole journey from struggle to shine.
origin: AAVE popularized on social media, widely adopted by hip-hop culture.
example_lines: From the bando to the penthouse — that's the ultimate glow up

definition: To successfully obtain money, a deal, or any form of valuable compensation. 'Securing the bag' is the primary motivation for hustlers and artists alike.
origin: National hip-hop and AAVE slang. Popularized in the mid-2010s.
example_lines: Signed the deal, secured the bag — now we eat for real

definition: Assets and money passed down through families — breaking the cycle of poverty. In rap, building generational wealth is the highest form of success beyond personal spending.
origin: Financial term that became central to hip-hop consciousness, especially post-2010s.
example_lines: The goal ain't just the Rollie — it's generational wealth so the kids never want

definition: Someone who has been with you since the beginning — before the fame, before the money, before anyone cared. A 'day one' is the highest form of loyalty.
origin: Universal hip-hop slang. The concept of ride-or-die loyalty from before success is central to rap's value system.
example_lines: He's my day one — we were in the bando together before any of this

definition: A person who betrays you while pretending to be loyal — a two-faced friend who stabs you in the back. Being called a snake is a serious accusation in hip-hop culture.
origin: Universal slang adopted widely in hip-hop.
example_lines: He's a snake — smiled in my face and went behind my back

definition: To keep it completely real — fully honest, transparent, and authentic. '100' means 100 percent genuine with no deception.
origin: AAVE and hip-hop slang. The 100 emoji became the digital shorthand.
example_lines: Keep it 100 with me — was that verse really you or did you get help?

definition: To handle your responsibilities with full commitment — to back up your words with action.
origin: Street culture and hip-hop. Popularized in the 2020s as a phrase about accountability.
example_lines: He said he'd respond and he did — stood on business

definition: An unspoken set of rules governing street life — don't snitch, don't fold, be loyal, handle business. The street equivalent of a chivalric code.
origin: Street culture. 'G' stands for gangster. A value system defining how real ones operate.
example_lines: He violated the G-code when he talked to investigators

definition: Low-quality, seedy, dry marijuana — the bottom of the weed quality hierarchy. The opposite of exotic or gas.
origin: National cannabis slang going back to at least the 90s.
example_lines: Ain't nobody smoking Reggie in this camp — gas only

definition: Someone who carries out violent acts on behalf of a gang, crew, or individual — an enforcer who pulls the trigger without hesitation.
origin: Street culture term universally used in hip-hop.
example_lines: He got money but he got shooters too — don't get it twisted

definition: The Italian luxury fashion house — in hip-hop, wearing a luxury fashion brand signals you've made it financially. Also used as an adjective meaning 'all good' or 'cool.'
origin: a luxury fashion brand Guccio, Florence Italy, 1921. In hip-hop adopted both as a brand reference and slang for everything being fine ('we're a luxury fashion brand').
example_lines: Head to toe a luxury fashion brand — the drip is immaculate
It's all a luxury fashion brand — no problems over here

definition: A New York skateboarding-turned-streetwear brand famous for its box logo and limited drops. a streetwear brand collaborations with a luxury fashion house and a major sportswear brand defined hype culture.
origin: James Jebbia, NYC, 1994. Originally a skateboarding brand that became the center of streetwear culture.
example_lines: Box logo hoodie — Supreme from the original Lafayette St. store

definition: A small corner store in New York City — a neighborhood staple that sells everything from food to loosies (individual cigarettes). The bodega is the social hub of NYC street life.
origin: Spanish word for storehouse/wine cellar. In NYC, the corner bodega is as culturally significant as any institution.
example_lines: Grabbed a loosie from the bodega and posted up on the corner

definition: A neighborhood on the east side of Atlanta — home to an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper. Zone 6 is one of Atlanta's most storied rap neighborhoods.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. Zone 6 refers to the city's postal/administrative zone system.
example_lines: Zone 6 baby — an Atlanta rapper said it best

definition: A member of the Nation of Gods and Earths — founded in Harlem in 1964, teaching that the Black man is God and knowledge of self is supreme. 5 Percenter theology is woven throughout golden era NYC rap.
origin: Nation of Gods and Earths, Harlem, 1964. Clarence 13X broke from the Nation of Islam. a Staten Island rap collective Clan, a pioneering MC, and Big Daddy Kane were influenced.
example_lines: His lyrics are deep with Five Percenter science — you need a glossary

definition: The New York City borough where hip-hop was born — DJ a founding DJ of hip-hop's 1973 block party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is considered hip-hop's origin point.
origin: The Bronx, New York City. August 11, 1973. DJ a founding DJ of hip-hop isolated the breakbeat and changed music forever.
example_lines: Every rapper owes a debt to the Bronx — that's where all of this began

definition: A historic neighborhood in northern Manhattan — home to the Harlem Renaissance, hip-hop's community roots, and artists like Cam'ron, Jim Jones, a Harlem rap group, and a Harlem rapper.
origin: New York City. The Harlem Renaissance established it as a cultural capital. Its contribution to hip-hop is immeasurable.
example_lines: Harlem made fashion rules before fashion knew what rules were

definition: A city in Los Angeles County — the birthplace of gangster rap. a founding West Coast rap group., a West Coast producer-rapper, a Compton rapper, a Compton rapper, and a dominant West Coast lyricist all claim Compton. Ground zero for West Coast hip-hop.
origin: Compton, California. a founding West Coast rap group's 'Straight Outta Compton' (1988) made it globally known. a dominant West Coast lyricist's 'good kid, m.A.A.d city' is the definitive Compton album.
example_lines: Straight outta Compton — the city that changed the entire direction of rap

definition: Personal style, charisma, and confidence — the way you carry yourself. Swag is the full package: clothes, attitude, walk, and energy all combined.
origin: Soulja Boy's 'Pretty Boy Swag' and a New Orleans rapper made it ubiquitous around 2009-2011.
example_lines: He walked in with swag before he said a word — the room felt it

definition: The collective social media practice of withdrawing support from public figures who have done something considered offensive. In hip-hop, attempted cancellation is often met with defiance.
origin: Social media era phenomenon, peaked in awareness around 2018-2020.
example_lines: They tried to cancel him but the fans didn't move — real ones don't fold

definition: A defined period in an artist's career or life — each era has its own sound, aesthetic, and emotional tone. Artists intentionally move from era to era as they grow.
origin: Music industry and fan culture term. Social media made 'eras' a conscious concept.
example_lines: This is his best era yet — the sound, the visuals, the energy all aligned

definition: An expanded edition of an album released after the original — usually adding 3-10 new tracks. Controversial because it can feel like content held back from the original release.
origin: Music industry marketing strategy. Became particularly prevalent in the streaming era.
example_lines: The deluxe dropped three weeks later and had the best song on it

definition: The original recording of a song — whoever owns the master owns the source and can license or withhold the music. Owning your masters is the ultimate music industry power move.
origin: Music industry term made culturally significant when Taylor Swift's masters were sold without her knowledge. a pioneering New York rapper and others made master ownership central to their business.
example_lines: He kept his masters — that's why he's still getting paid off records from 2007

definition: An artist's entire body of work — all albums, singles, and features. A deep catalog signals longevity and consistency. Owning your catalog means controlling your masters.
origin: Music industry term. A deep catalog is cited as evidence of GOAT status.
example_lines: His catalog is airtight — no skips from 2003 to now

definition: RIAA certification for selling one million units. In rap, going platinum is the benchmark of commercial success. Multi-platinum means multiple millions.
origin: RIAA (Recording Industry Association of America) certification.
example_lines: The debut went platinum in the first week — that's unheard of

definition: An artist or project that deserved more recognition than it received — underrated, overlooked by the mainstream. Being 'slept on' is almost a badge of honor in underground circles.
origin: Hip-hop slang for underappreciation. To 'sleep on' someone means to dismiss them.
example_lines: He was slept on for a decade — now everybody retroactively claims they knew

definition: The strategic marketing campaign leading up to an album release — the sequence of singles, interviews, features, and social media moments that build anticipation.
origin: Music industry marketing term.
example_lines: The rollout was flawless — every drop landed perfectly

definition: Your tight inner circle — closer than a crew but smaller. The clique is the core group that matters most, the ones you share everything with.
origin: French word for a group, adopted into hip-hop vernacular.
example_lines: My clique don't miss — everybody eats or nobody eats

definition: Keeping something secret or under the radar — doing things quietly without broadcasting your moves. 'On the low' is discretion as a survival skill.
origin: Universal AAVE adopted into hip-hop. Essential to both street life and industry navigation.
example_lines: We moving on the low — no social media, no announcements

definition: Subtle, understated, or secret. 'Lowkey' means doing something without drawing attention, or admitting something you'd rather not announce publicly.
origin: National slang that became universal in hip-hop. Often used to admit things you'd rather not say outright.
example_lines: Lowkey that album was better than people give it credit for

definition: The opposite of lowkey — obviously, publicly, without restraint. 'Highkey' means something you're openly admitting or doing without shame.
origin: Internet slang adopted into hip-hop discourse. The antonym of lowkey.
example_lines: Highkey this is the best album they ever made — I'll say it out loud

definition: A cultural movement, trend, or energy that sweeps through hip-hop. To be 'on the wave' means you're riding the current trend. To 'start a wave' is to be the originator.
origin: Popularized by a Harlem rap collective and a Harlem rapper's crew in the early 2010s. 'Wave' as a concept in cultural leadership.
example_lines: He started the wave and now everybody biting his style

definition: Style combined with ease — effortless cool. 'Steeze' is a mashup of 'style' and 'ease.' If you have steeze, your whole vibe looks natural, not forced.
origin: New York hip-hop slang, popularized in the skateboarding and hip-hop communities of the 90s.
example_lines: You can't teach steeze — either you got it or you don't

definition: An outfit — short for 'fit.' A 'fit check' is when someone shows off what they're wearing. A good fit is a carefully curated head-to-toe look.
origin: Shortened from 'outfit.' Became standard in streetwear and hip-hop culture in the 2010s.
example_lines: The fit was hard — everything coordinated perfectly

definition: To verify that all money is accounted for after a transaction or deal. Also metaphorically used to mean double-checking your finances or ensuring you're paid correctly.
origin: Street and business culture. In hip-hop, checking the bag means being financially diligent and not getting played.
example_lines: Before you sign anything, check the bag — read every line

definition: To make a bold, risky attempt at something — asking someone out, pitching a deal, or sending a cold DM. If it doesn't work, you took your shot and that's respectable.
origin: Basketball terminology adopted into hip-hop and dating culture.
example_lines: He shot his shot at the label and they actually responded

definition: A Glock handgun — the most referenced firearm in hip-hop. Glock became synonymous with handguns in general through trap and drill music.
origin: Glock GmbH, Austria. The Glock 17 (1982) became the most popular handgun in America and consequently the most referenced gun in hip-hop.
example_lines: Glock on the hip, just in case the opps feel brave tonight

definition: A gun — any firearm but most commonly a handgun. 'Strapping' means carrying a weapon.
origin: Street slang adopted universally in hip-hop across all regions and eras.
example_lines: He was strapped the whole time — nobody knew

definition: Conversation that only makes sense between people in the drug trade — coded language, numbers, and references that outsiders won't understand.
origin: Drug trade culture. Used in trap music to reference conversations with suppliers without being obvious.
example_lines: That whole verse is plug talk — need a translation guide

definition: The fee an artist charges to appear on another rapper's song. Feature prices range from free (for friends) to hundreds of thousands for major artists.
origin: Music industry practice. Feature price became a cultural conversation when artists started publicizing or leaking their rates.
example_lines: His feature price is so high most labels can't afford a verse

definition: A reference to the popular rap interview podcast hosted by Adam22 — known for raw, unfiltered conversations with rappers. Also means no hesitation to jump into action.
origin: a hip-hop podcast podcast, founded by Adam22 in 2015. Became one of the most influential rap media outlets.
example_lines: He did the a hip-hop podcast interview and said everything — no filter

definition: A verbal attack or insult aimed at another rapper — through lyrics, interviews, or social media. Every major beef involves disses. Short for 'disrespect.'
origin: Short for 'disrespect.' Core vocabulary in hip-hop beef culture since the Roxanne Wars.
example_lines: He dropped a diss that ended the beef immediately — nothing to respond to

definition: A song made specifically to answer a diss — the battle rap equivalent of a reply. Response tracks need to come fast and hit harder than the original to win.
origin: Battle rap and beef culture. Every great diss in hip-hop has prompted response tracks.
example_lines: The response track came 48 hours later — he was ready

definition: A subtle lyrical attack aimed at someone without naming them — leaving just enough clues that the target and insiders understand the message but maintaining plausible deniability.
origin: Rap beef tactic. Allows artists to take shots without fully committing to a public beef.
example_lines: That was a subliminal shot — he didn't say a name but the whole industry knew who it was for

definition: An overwhelming quantity of quality lyrical content — bar after bar of elite writing. No filler, no hooks that save weak verses.
origin: Hip-hop appreciator slang for lyrical density and consistency.
example_lines: Bars on bars on bars — you can't play this album casual, you gotta study it

definition: The clever manipulation of language — using words with double meanings, homophones, and creative associations to pack more into a line than it first appears to contain.
origin: Poetic technique. In hip-hop, wordplay is one of the most appreciated technical skills.
example_lines: His wordplay is next level — every bar has multiple meanings hidden in it

definition: Rapping without any preparation or written material — purely improvising from memory and real-time creativity.
origin: Hip-hop slang for improvised performance. 'The dome' = your head.
example_lines: He went off the dome for 20 minutes and didn't miss once

definition: Rapping — delivering lyrics with energy and force. 'Spit a verse' means rap a verse. One of the most common verbs in hip-hop vocabulary.
origin: Universal hip-hop slang. The physicality of rapping — projecting words with force.
example_lines: He was spitting fire the whole show — didn't even break a sweat

definition: A rhyme scheme — the pattern of rhyming sounds in a rap verse. Advanced rappers use complex, multi-bar schemes that pay off lines later.
origin: Poetic term adapted for hip-hop. Having a 'tight scheme' means your rhymes are organized and deliberate.
example_lines: His rhyme scheme doesn't pay off until the third bar — that's advanced writing

definition: The technique of spending 1-2 bars establishing a premise before delivering the knockout line. The setup makes the punchline land harder.
origin: Comedy technique brought into hip-hop. The best battle rappers are masters of setup and delivery.
example_lines: That whole first bar was the setup — the punchline on bar two sent the room wild

definition: The period (roughly 2005-2015) when free mixtapes distributed online were more culturally important than studio albums — when rappers built their reputations through volume and quality of free music.
origin: Physical mixtape tradition evolved to digital. a mixtape platform and LiveMixtapes were the platforms that defined the era.
example_lines: The mixtape era produced some of the greatest rap music ever made — all free

definition: A project released independently without major label infrastructure — raw, unpolished, and aimed at the streets rather than radio. Often more respected than the label debut that follows.
origin: Hip-hop tradition of independent releases. a Philadelphia rapper, Wale, and others dropped street albums before major deals.
example_lines: The street album was better than anything the label released — that's always how it goes

definition: A public endorsement or stamp of approval from an established artist — when someone with credibility vouches for a new artist's talent. A co-sign can launch a career.
origin: Hip-hop culture. From the financial term 'co-signing' a loan — you're putting your name behind someone else.
example_lines: He got the co-sign from an OG and everything changed overnight

definition: Detroit, Michigan — a city with a rich hip-hop history led by a Detroit rapper, a Detroit rapper, and Danny Brown. Detroit rap has a gritty, industrial sound that reflects the city's manufacturing legacy.
origin: Detroit, Michigan. a Detroit rapper put Detroit on the global map. Royce da 5'9", a Detroit rapper, Doughboyz Cashout, and others continue the tradition.
example_lines: Detroit built a Detroit rapper and a Detroit rapper built Detroit's place in hip-hop — a full circle

definition: A location — usually an abandoned or rented property — where drugs are cooked, packaged, and sold. The nerve center of the trap economy.
origin: Atlanta, Georgia. an Atlanta rapper popularized the concept nationally with 'Trap Muzik' (2003). an Atlanta rapper's early career was built around trap house realism.
example_lines: The trap house never slept — 24 hours, no days off

definition: To sell drugs to customers — 'serving' means completing a drug transaction. 'The block was getting served' means drugs were being sold there.
origin: Drug trade terminology universally adopted in hip-hop.
example_lines: He was serving the whole block before he turned 18

definition: Your neighborhood — specifically the immediate streets where you grew up and operate. 'The block' is community, identity, and responsibility all in one.
origin: Universal street culture. In hip-hop, 'the block' represents origin, loyalty, and duty to your community.
example_lines: Everything I do is for the block — that's where it started and that's where I stay rooted

definition: Your neighborhood — with the understanding that it's impoverished, underserved, and shaped by struggle. The hood is where many rappers come from and maintain loyalty to.
origin: Short for 'neighborhood.' Used universally in hip-hop to describe low-income urban areas.
example_lines: The hood made me who I am — I can't disconnect from that even if I wanted to

definition: Public housing complexes — government-funded apartment buildings where many hip-hop artists grew up. 'The projects' represent the starting point for countless rap careers.
origin: Public housing policy in the US. Places like Marcy Houses (a pioneering New York rapper), Queensbridge (a Queensbridge MC), and Jordan Downs (a West Coast MC) are iconic projects.
example_lines: From the projects to the penthouse — that's the American dream nobody shows you how to do

definition: The largest public housing complex in the United States — located in Long Island City, Queens, NYC. Home to a Queensbridge MC, Mobb Deep, Nature, and many others. The most musically significant housing project in history.
origin: Queensbridge Houses, Queens, New York. a Queensbridge MC's 'Illmatic' immortalized Queensbridge.
example_lines: Queensbridge produced more classic rap than most cities combined — QB all day

definition: The Marcy Houses — a public housing project in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn. a pioneering New York rapper grew up here and has referenced it throughout his career. One of hip-hop's most iconic addresses.
origin: Marcy Houses, Brooklyn, New York. a pioneering New York rapper's 'Marcy Me' and countless other references made it legendary.
example_lines: Marcy raised a pioneering New York rapper — that says everything you need to know about what that block produces

definition: A city in Los Angeles County adjacent to Compton — home to Nipsey Hussle, Dom Kennedy, and others. Inglewood represents a quieter but equally important thread of West Coast rap culture.
origin: Inglewood, California. Nipsey Hussle's Marathon Clothing Store and Slauson Ave connections made Inglewood globally significant.
example_lines: Inglewood always up to no good — and Nipsey made sure the whole world knew about it

definition: New Orleans, Louisiana — home to a New Orleans label Records, a New Orleans rapper, Juvenile, Master P, a New Orleans label Records, and Birdman. The Dirty South sound started here. A city whose music culture is as important as its food culture.
origin: New Orleans, Louisiana. a New Orleans label and a New Orleans label Records defined Southern rap in the late 90s and early 2000s.
example_lines: New Orleans gave hip-hop a New Orleans label and a New Orleans rapper — that alone is an eternal contribution

definition: Miami, Florida — home to the bass music movement, a Miami rapper, Flo Rida, Pitbull, and a distinct South Florida hip-hop sound. Miami bass influenced trap and electronic music globally.
origin: Miami, Florida. Miami bass (2 Live Crew) in the 80s-90s, then a Miami rapper in the 2000s put Miami on the hip-hop map.
example_lines: Miami bass changed the 808 game before trap even existed — the South was always first

definition: A subgenre blending trap music with R&B sensibilities — heavy 808s, melodic singing, and vulnerable emotional content. Bryson Tiller is credited with naming and defining the genre.
origin: Bryson Tiller's 'T R A P S O U L' (2015) formally named the genre that artists like an Atlanta rapper, a prominent Toronto-based rapper, and PartyNextDoor were already creating.
example_lines: That whole album is trap soul — it hits harder than trap and softer than R&B at the same time

definition: A pejorative term for rap with deliberately unintelligible or unclear lyrics — associated with the an online streaming platform rap era. Critics use it dismissively; many artists embrace the aesthetic intentionally.
origin: Coined as a criticism in the mid-2010s as melodic, AutoTune-heavy trap from an online streaming platform became dominant.
example_lines: He called it mumble rap but the fans called it a movement — perspective is everything

definition: A wave of artists who built massive audiences on an online streaming platform before any major label interest — characterized by distorted 808s, face tattoos, and emo/punk influences mixed with trap.
origin: an online streaming platform platform. Peaked 2015-2018. XXXTentacion, Lil Pump, and a Chicago rapper are key figures.
example_lines: an online streaming platform rap changed the gatekeeping — you didn't need a label to reach millions anymore

definition: Pitch correction software that became a creative tool in hip-hop — T-Pain pioneered using it as an effect rather than hiding it. an Atlanta rapper, an Atlanta rapper, and a Houston rapper made AutoTune-as-instrument standard.
origin: Antares Audio Technologies, 1997. T-Pain's 'Busted' (2005) made AutoTune a deliberate artistic choice.
example_lines: AutoTune went from a cheat code to an instrument — T-Pain deserves royalties from every trap song

definition: Referring to the Roland TR-808's legendary bass drum or to the emotional weight of 808-driven music. a Chicago producer-rapper's 'heartbreak' era and trap music made 808s emotional, not just rhythmic.
origin: Roland TR-808, 1980. a Chicago producer-rapper West's '808s & Heartbreak' (2008) made the 808 a symbol of vulnerability in rap.
example_lines: The 808 on that track hit so deep it felt personal — that's the power of the drum machine

definition: Having an endless supply of quality lyrics — so much good material that it seems inexhaustible. A compliment for rappers who never seem to run out of heat.
origin: Universal hip-hop slang for lyrical abundance.
example_lines: He's got bars for days — three albums in and he hasn't slowed down at all

definition: To speak your truth without restraint — saying exactly what you think with complete confidence, regardless of how it lands. Often means bragging or being direct about your superiority.
origin: AAVE and hip-hop slang. 'Talking your shit' is about unfiltered self-expression.
example_lines: He gets on the mic and talks his shit — no holding back, no filter, no apologies

definition: A declaration that you and your crew are out in the world, showing up, and actively present. Also means it's time to celebrate — the party is here, the vibe is live.
origin: AAVE and social media era slang. Popularized in the early 2020s.
example_lines: Album dropped and it's number one — we outside tonight, no excuses

definition: To perfectly execute what was needed — to show up exactly right for the moment, sound, or vibe. A high compliment for a rapper who delivered exactly what a project required.
origin: Internet slang that became universal in the early 2020s.
example_lines: He understood the assignment on that feature — matched the energy and elevated it

definition: Hip-hop and Black culture as a whole — the shared values, aesthetics, music, and community that hip-hop represents. 'The culture' is treated with reverence as something larger than any individual.
origin: Hip-hop philosophy. 'The culture' as a concept positions hip-hop as a living, breathing entity that must be respected and protected.
example_lines: He violated the culture with that move — some things you just don't do

definition: Your watch — specifically how your watch looks on your wrist. 'The wrist is frozen' means your watch is iced out. 'Looking at the wrist' is a flex move.
origin: Hip-hop shorthand for watch flex. Used in countless rap lyrics as a substitute for naming the watch brand.
example_lines: The wrist on froze — couldn't see the diamonds if you tried

definition: Having such an extreme level of fashion and style that it's overwhelming — beyond normal drip levels. The phrase was popularized by an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper's song of the same name.
origin: an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper, 'Drip Too Hard' (2018). Became a universal compliment for extreme style.
example_lines: The fit is dripping too hard — the whole room is wet just from looking at him

definition: Someone whose sauce (style, charisma, effortless cool) is at a divine level — a god among the sauced. Used both seriously and humorously.
origin: Atlanta trap culture. The 'sauce god' persona developed through an Atlanta rapper, Offset, and the broader ATL aesthetic.
example_lines: He walked in the room and everybody saw it — that's a sauce god energy

definition: The absolute highest level of quality — beyond elite, beyond great, at a level that seems supernatural. Reserved for the very best of anything in hip-hop.
origin: Gaming and internet culture term adopted into hip-hop. Used to describe artists, beats, verses, or fashion that exceed normal standards.
example_lines: That verse is god tier — put it in the archive next to the classics

definition: An album released with only the main artist and no guest appearances — considered the highest test of an artist's solo ability. Also a flex that your catalog doesn't need anyone else.
origin: Music industry term. Some of the greatest rap albums had no features (Illmatic, The Chronic).
example_lines: He dropped a no features project and it still went platinum — that's different

definition: To be in a state of intense creative productivity — making music at a high level and high volume. 'In the kitchen' means in the studio; 'cooking' means creating heat.
origin: Metaphor from cooking/baking. Used in hip-hop to describe intense creative sessions.
example_lines: He's been cooking all year — ten projects since January, each one harder than the last

definition: P stands for 'player' — push P means to push positivity, to keep it real, to be genuine and build something real. an Atlanta rapper made this phrase massive in early 2022.
origin: an Atlanta rapper and an Atlanta rapper popularized 'pushin P' as a phrase in early 2022. It became a cultural moment.
example_lines: Bought a house for the family — that's pushin P, no cap

definition: You successfully got the money, deal, or opportunity you were pursuing. The bag is in hand — mission accomplished.
origin: Evolved from 'secure the bag.' Became its own confirmation phrase in the 2010s-2020s.
example_lines: Signed the publishing deal, bag secured — three generations will eat off this

definition: Your enemies trying to contact you through social media — usually to start drama, gather information, or instigate. A modern manifestation of the opp dynamic.
origin: Social media era. As beef moved partially online, 'opps in the DMs' became a real thing rappers experienced.
example_lines: Opps in the DMs acting friendly — nah, I see through the moves

definition: A project that may not have charted commercially but is universally respected and referenced on the streets — proof that the culture moves independently of the charts.
origin: Hip-hop culture. The 'streets' have always had their own criteria for what's classic, separate from commercial success.
example_lines: That tape is a certified street classic — every hood knows every word but it never went gold

definition: A defining moment of complete public destruction in a beef — named after a Queensbridge MC's 'Ether' diss. When someone has an ether moment, the conversation is over and they won decisively.
origin: Derived from a Queensbridge MC's 'Ether' (2001). Any diss or response that permanently damages someone's reputation is called an ether moment.
example_lines: That diss track was his ether moment — the other side went quiet for two years

definition: A phrase declaring superiority and distinctiveness — 'not like us' means you operate on a different level than those around you. Popularized as a diss track title by a dominant West Coast lyricist in 2024.
origin: Became massive as the title of a dominant West Coast lyricist's 2024 diss targeting a prominent Toronto-based rapper — arguably the most impactful diss track in 25 years.
example_lines: He dropped 'Not Like Us' and the cultural conversation shifted overnight — history made

definition: Saying something officially and permanently — as if it's been recorded to vinyl and can't be taken back. 'Putting it on wax' means you've committed your words to a permanent record.
origin: From the era of vinyl records — pressing a record is a permanent, public act. In hip-hop, going 'on wax' about someone means you've made it official.
example_lines: He said it on wax — can't take it back now, the record exists forever

definition: Complete dismissal — refusing to acknowledge an excuse, explanation, or response. Used to shut down arguments or deflect weak comebacks.
origin: Universal AAVE. Used in hip-hop as a response to weak disses or excuses.
example_lines: He came with a response and the whole internet said 'I ain't tryna hear that'

definition: To end something — a conversation, a beef, a situation. 'Dead that' is an order to stop and move on.
origin: New York City slang. Part of NYC's direct, cut-to-the-chase communication style.
example_lines: Dead that noise — the conversation is over, next topic

definition: To resolve a conflict — both parties agree to end the hostilities and move forward. Squashing beef can be done publicly (through handshakes or collab tracks) or privately.
origin: Universal hip-hop slang. The opposite of escalating beef — to squash means to end it.
example_lines: They squashed the beef at the listening party — dapped up in front of everybody

definition: An acknowledgment that quality lyrical content is quality regardless of who delivered it — even if it came from someone you have beef with.
origin: Universal hip-hop expression of respect for craft above personal feelings.
example_lines: I don't like him personally but bars is bars — that verse was hard

definition: Bars or a verse that is so intense and lyrically dense it puts metaphorical 'pressure' on the listener or opponent.
origin: Widespread hip-hop slang.
example_lines: He came with pressure on that track — nobody was ready

definition: Style, swag, or a certain undeniable cool factor that's hard to define but instantly recognizable.
origin: Southern hip-hop, popularized early 2010s.
example_lines: Dripping in sauce before it was fashionable

definition: Truthfully; without exaggeration. Assertion that what is being said is completely honest.
origin: Atlanta slang, popularized mid-2010s via rap.
example_lines: This the hardest album of the year, no cap

definition: A lie or exaggeration. To 'cap' is to lie.
origin: Atlanta slang, went national via rap in the 2010s.
example_lines: Stop capping — you were never in those streets

definition: Exciting, fun, high-energy; a party or moment that is going exceptionally well.
origin: African American slang, popularized in rap mid-2010s.
example_lines: The section was lit from the jump

definition: Highly energized, intoxicated, or in a state of intense excitement, usually at a party or event.
origin: Southern slang, popularized by rap in early 2010s.
example_lines: We were turnt the whole night, no breaks

definition: Fire; exceptionally good. Common Southern pronunciation/spelling of 'fire.'
origin: Southern hip-hop, particularly Atlanta.
example_lines: That beat is fye, he needs that one

definition: Describes music that sounds extremely good, especially with bass — it 'slaps' in the car.
origin: West Coast slang, widely adopted.
example_lines: This project slaps front to back, no skips

definition: Music that hits hard in a car system; bass-heavy tracks that physically knock.
origin: Bay Area/West Coast slang.
example_lines: Throw that in the whip — it knocks

definition: Immediate confrontation or action upon seeing someone — no conversation, no delay.
origin: Street slang adopted widely in hip-hop.
example_lines: After what he did, it's on sight if I catch him

definition: To go confront someone; to pull up on an enemy location.
origin: Chicago drill slang, spread nationally via rap.
example_lines: They slid through and the whole block scattered

definition: A Chicago street term for gang activity; also the name of the subgenre that emerged from Chicago in the early 2010s characterized by dark, trap-influenced beats and street narratives.
origin: Chicago, early 2010s. Chief Keef, G Herbo, a Chicago rapper's early circle.
example_lines: He really from the drill — been moving since day one

definition: Enemies; opposition; people who are actively against you or your crew.
origin: Chicago drill slang, now universal in hip-hop.
example_lines: The ops been lurking so we don't move sloppy

definition: Influence, fame, or social status — especially online. To have 'clout' is to have people paying attention to you.
origin: Hip-hop and social media, went mainstream mid-2010s.
example_lines: He only did that for clout — no principles

definition: Someone who associates with famous people or does controversial things purely to gain attention and followers.
origin: Internet/hip-hop culture, 2010s.
example_lines: She a clout chaser — wasn't around when he was unknown

definition: Either actual violence or devastatingly effective verses — to 'body' a track is to deliver an outstanding performance; 'bodies' can refer to street violence.
origin: Hip-hop slang with street origins.
example_lines: He bodied every verse on that feature run

definition: To be lyrically destroyed in a diss track — named after a Queensbridge MC's legendary diss 'Ether' (2001).
origin: Named after a Queensbridge MC's 2001 track 'Ether,' considered one of the greatest diss records.
example_lines: He got ethered on wax and never fully recovered

definition: To completely dominate a situation, track, or scene — seizing control through skill or force.
origin: Hip-hop slang with cultural references to a pioneering New York rapper's 2001 diss 'The Takeover.'
example_lines: The new generation is staging a full takeover of the rap game

definition: The overall feeling or energy of a place, situation, or piece of music. A good vibe = positive energy.
origin: African American slang, adopted universally via hip-hop.
example_lines: The studio session had the right vibe — album came out crazy

definition: A cultural movement or trend; to be 'on the wave' is to be ahead of or part of a rising cultural shift.
origin: New York/a Harlem rap collective popularized the term in 2010s hip-hop.
example_lines: He started the wave before everybody caught on

definition: A catchy, enjoyable song — usually upbeat and radio-friendly rather than lyric-heavy.
origin: African American slang, popularized in hip-hop and R&B.
example_lines: That's a bop — going to be stuck in your head all week

definition: A guest appearance on a song by an artist who is not the primary performer.
origin: Standard music industry term embedded deeply in hip-hop culture.
example_lines: His feature rate is astronomical but it's worth every penny

definition: Reusing the melody or lyrics of an existing song but re-recording it rather than sampling the original master.
origin: Music production and copyright law term, central to hip-hop sample culture.
example_lines: They interpolated the hook and avoided the sample clearance fee

definition: How often listeners return to a song or album; a measure of quality and depth beyond first impressions.
origin: Music criticism term adopted in hip-hop culture.
example_lines: The album has crazy replay value — something new every listen

definition: A skilled lyricist who crafts words with precision and artistry.
origin: Classic hip-hop term of respect for elite lyricists.
example_lines: He's a true wordsmith — every line has multiple readings

definition: The climactic, impactful line in a verse — usually at the end of a bar sequence — designed to land with maximum effect.
origin: Comedy term adapted by hip-hop to describe clever or hard-hitting bar endings.
example_lines: He builds the setup for four bars just to land one devastating punchline

definition: Double or triple meanings embedded in a single line — a hallmark of elite lyricism.
origin: French linguistic term adopted by hip-hop lyricists.
example_lines: That bar has at least three entendres — took me a week to catch them all

definition: Short for multisyllabic rhymes — rhyming multiple syllables across words in the same bar or across bars.
origin: Lyrical hip-hop technique term.
example_lines: His multis are insane — three-syllable rhymes for sixteen bars straight

definition: Rhymes that occur within a single bar rather than only at the end of lines.
origin: Advanced lyrical technique in hip-hop.
example_lines: His internal rhymes pack more content into one bar than most rappers put in a verse

definition: An album built around a central theme, story, or idea where songs connect as a cohesive artistic statement.
origin: Rock music term that became central to hip-hop's most ambitious projects.
example_lines: That concept album changed how people thought about what rap could do

definition: Authenticated as the real thing; a person, product, or record that has proven itself genuine.
origin: RIAA certification for sales, but in hip-hop slang means authenticity.
