example_lines: He's certified in these streets — been here since before the cameras

definition: The highest level of street or cultural credibility granted to someone who has been around longest and earned respect through experience.
origin: OG (Original Gangster) concept from gang culture adopted by hip-hop.
example_lines: He's got OG status in this city — nobody questions his position

definition: The early 2020s resurgence of interest in 90s-style hip-hop production — hard drums, jazz samples, lyric-focused.
origin: Cultural reaction to melodic/mumble rap dominance.
example_lines: The boom bap revival proved there's always hunger for real lyrics

definition: Plays on a streaming service, a streaming service, etc. — became the primary metric for commercial success after downloads replaced physical sales.
origin: Music industry shift, 2010s.
example_lines: He doesn't care about streaming numbers — he tours and merchandise

definition: Songs designed or promoted primarily for social media virality — often short hooks, trending sounds, or challenge-worthy moments.
origin: social media platform dominance, 2019-present.
example_lines: The social media rap era made catchiness more important than longevity

definition: Slang for the network of underground venues, labels, and platforms that support non-commercial rap artists.
origin: Hip-hop culture, metaphor from American history.
example_lines: He moved through the underground railroad for a decade before mainstream noticed him

definition: Consecutive, relentless bars delivered without filler — sustained excellence throughout a verse or song.
origin: Universal hip-hop expression.
example_lines: That freestyle was bars on bars — he didn't miss once

definition: The craft of writing rap lyrics with precision and artistry — a rapper's writing skill and style on paper.
origin: Classic hip-hop term emphasizing rap as a written art form.
example_lines: His penmanship is unmatched — every line earns its place

definition: A freestyle rap session where artists take turns rapping in a circle, often competitive and improvisational.
origin: Old school hip-hop practice, deeply tied to b-boy and early MC culture.
example_lines: The cipher outside the park was where reputations got made or destroyed

definition: Pre-written rap verses, as opposed to freestyles. A 'written' is a prepared and crafted verse.
origin: Hip-hop distinction between improvised and composed rap.
example_lines: He came with writtens to the freestyle battle — people caught on quick

definition: Classic robbery demand — 'hand over your jewelry.' Also refers to the crew/duo RTJ (El-P and Killer Mike), formed 2013.
origin: 90s New York robbery culture slang, reclaimed by Run the Jewels duo.
example_lines: Run the jewels — that's the threat and the name at the same time

definition: To remain armed at all times; to always carry a weapon.
origin: Street/gang culture, adopted into hip-hop vocabulary.
example_lines: In his neighborhood you stay strapped or you stay humble

definition: A a New Orleans label Records term originating from the Hot Boys group (Juvenile, a New Orleans rapper, B.G., Turk) — a young, flashy, street-active male.
origin: a New Orleans label Records, New Orleans, late 90s.
example_lines: He came up in an era when being a hot boy meant staying dangerous and fly simultaneously

definition: Late 90s to mid-2000s period characterized by extreme displays of jewelry, diamonds, and material wealth in hip-hop culture.
origin: Popularized by a New Orleans label Records and B.G.'s 'Bling Bling' (1999).
example_lines: The bling era produced some of the most over-the-top jewelry moments in rap history

definition: A Southern hip-hop subgenre and lifestyle term meaning hyped up, wild, energetic — pioneered by an Atlanta producer-rapper in the early 2000s.
origin: Atlanta, early 2000s. an Atlanta producer-rapper & the East Side Boyz defined the sound and term.
example_lines: The crunk era made Atlanta clubs the center of the rap universe for a minute

definition: Bay Area culture and music movement — hyperactive, wild, and free-spirited. Associated with ghost riding and going dumb.
origin: Bay Area, California. E-40, Too $hort, Mistah F.A.B., mid-2000s.
example_lines: The hyphy movement never got its full mainstream due, but it influenced everything

definition: Bay Area term for going crazy on the dance floor or behaving wildly without inhibition.
origin: Bay Area hyphy culture, mid-2000s.
example_lines: When that beat drops, the whole crowd goes dumb

definition: A Houston production technique of slowing down music and adding stuttered effects — created by DJ Screw in the 90s.
origin: Houston, Texas. DJ Screw originated the technique in Screwed Up Click parties.
example_lines: Hearing that album chopped and screwed is a completely different emotional experience

definition: Authentic reputation earned through lived street experience — separate from fame or money, harder to fake.
origin: Core concept in hip-hop culture separating authentic artists from pretenders.
example_lines: No amount of bars can manufacture street credibility you never earned

definition: 2000s-2010s period when rappers distributed free mixtapes to build buzz before albums — an essential path to rap stardom.
origin: New York origins, expanded nationally. DJ Drama's a DJ-hosted mixtape series was foundational.
example_lines: The mixtape era created careers that the label system wouldn't have allowed

definition: The Roland TR-808 drum machine whose bass drum sound became foundational to hip-hop and trap production.
origin: Roland TR-808 synthesizer/drum machine, widely used in hip-hop since the 80s.
example_lines: The 808s on that track hit so hard it felt like a physical impact

definition: Rapid cymbal sounds in trap and hip-hop production — the triplet hi-hats (rolling hi-hats) are a defining sound of modern trap.
origin: Drum production terminology, central to trap music sound.
example_lines: The triplet hi-hats on that beat made it feel like it was sprinting

definition: A rhythmic technique where the rapper delivers three syllables per beat instead of two, creating a rolling, cascading cadence.
origin: Popularized in trap era, though the technique has earlier roots.
example_lines: He switched to triplet flow mid-verse and the whole energy shifted

definition: Improvised vocal exclamations and interjections throughout a rap track — a rapper's signature sound markers.
origin: Music term embedded in hip-hop culture, every major rapper has signature adlibs.
example_lines: You can identify him in five seconds just from the adlibs

definition: Style of rapping that uses Auto-Tune pitch correction as an artistic effect rather than to hide pitch issues — creating a melodic, sometimes robotic sound.
origin: T-Pain popularized deliberately artistic Auto-Tune in mid-2000s. an Atlanta rapper and a Houston rapper refined it.
example_lines: Auto-tune rap gets dismissed by purists but it takes real musicality to use it effectively

definition: A rapper who elevates street narratives to literary art through vivid imagery, metaphor, and emotional depth.
origin: Respect term in hip-hop for artists who transcend simple street reporting.
example_lines: He's not just rapping about the hood — he's a street poet mapping the human cost of it

definition: A short comedic or narrative interlude on an album — not a full song. Skits set the mood, add storytelling, or give the artist's crew a moment. Golden era albums used them heavily between tracks.
origin: Theater/comedy term brought into hip-hop albums in the early 90s to add texture and personality between songs.
example_lines: The skit had the whole crew laughing before the next track dropped

definition: A short transitional track on an album — usually under two minutes — used to bridge themes, moods, or storylines between full songs.
origin: Classical music term adopted by hip-hop and R&B for album sequencing and narrative flow.
example_lines: That interlude set up the next song perfectly

definition: The closing section of a song or album. An outro can be an extended last verse, a fading monologue, or an instrumental wind-down. Often where rappers leave their most raw, unguarded thoughts.
origin: Opposite of intro. Became common in hip-hop as artists started treating albums as complete works with deliberate endings.
example_lines: He bodied the outro harder than the whole song
The outro hit different after you hear the whole album

definition: Physically searching through bins of vinyl records looking for obscure samples, rare grooves, or forgotten classics. The foundation of hip-hop production — the best beats came from producers who dug deepest.
origin: Refers to the literal milk crates used to store vinyl in used record stores. A core practice since hip-hop's founding.
example_lines: He spent all Saturday crate digging and found the perfect sample
Real producers crate dig — they don't just use drum kits

definition: A recording technique where the artist records in short bursts — a few bars at a time — rather than one full take. Common in the trap era. Critics say it breaks flow; defenders say it produces sharper delivery.
origin: Studio engineering term. Became widespread in the 2010s as DAW recording replaced booth-style takes.
example_lines: He punches in every 4 bars — never does full takes
You can tell he punched in on that verse

definition: Rapping with no beat — voice only. Used in ciphers, showcases, and as a test of pure skill. If you can hold a crowd acapella, your pen and delivery are undeniable.
origin: Italian for 'in the manner of the chapel' — choral singing without instruments. Adopted by hip-hop for unaccompanied rap performances.
example_lines: He rocked the whole park acapella and the crowd still went crazy

definition: 1. To reinterpret a sample — chop it, pitch it, and rebuild it into something new. 2. To turn a small investment into a larger profit. Both meanings involve transforming something raw into something valuable.
origin: Dual street and music term. In production, flipping a sample is the art of making it unrecognizable from its source.
example_lines: He flipped that old soul record into something completely different
Put $500 in, flipped it to five racks

definition: To cut a sample into small pieces and rearrange them rhythmically — a production technique that transforms a recognizable loop into something entirely new. Chopping is a core skill in Southern and sample-based production.
origin: Production technique refined in Houston's chopped and screwed culture and in broader hip-hop sampling.
example_lines: He chopped that vocal sample so hard you can't even tell what song it's from

definition: A repeated musical phrase — usually 2 or 4 bars of a sample — that forms the foundation of a beat. Early hip-hop was almost entirely loop-based. A great loop can carry a whole song.
origin: Tape loop technique from early sampling. DJs used two copies of a record to extend the best 8 bars indefinitely.
example_lines: That loop is so hard it doesn't even need drums
He let the loop breathe and it hit harder for it

definition: The sharp, cracking drum hit — usually on beats 2 and 4 — that drives the rhythm of a rap beat. In trap, the snare is often layered, reverbed, or delayed for a rolling effect. The snare tells you where the pocket is.
origin: Acoustic drum term. Central to hip-hop production since the genre's founding.
example_lines: That snare is cracking like a gunshot
The snare roll at the end of every bar is the whole vibe

definition: The bass drum hit in a beat — deep, punchy, and felt as much as heard. Works together with the 808 in trap. In boom bap, the kick and snare combo is everything.
origin: Acoustic drum term. The kick pattern defines the groove of a hip-hop beat.
example_lines: That kick is knocking so hard I can feel it in my chest

definition: A specific approach or strategy in a battle rap — attacking an opponent's appearance, reputation, personal life, or past bars. Choosing the right angle can win or lose a battle before you even start rapping.
origin: Battle rap strategy term. The best battlers research opponents and build devastating angles.
example_lines: He had the wrong angle — came with gun bars when he should've gone personal
Find the right angle and you win before you even open your mouth

definition: Forgetting your lyrics under pressure — the worst thing that can happen in a battle or live performance. One choke can end a career in battle rap. Even elite rappers have choked under pressure.
origin: Sports term applied to performance pressure. In battle rap, choking is catastrophic and opponents never let you forget it.
example_lines: He choked in the third round and never recovered
Don't choke when the crowd is watching

definition: An especially powerful, devastating punchline — the kind that ends the conversation. A haymaker doesn't just score points, it puts the opponent on the floor. The crowd goes silent before the reaction.
origin: Boxing term for a wild, devastating punch. Applied to battle rap for lines that are impossible to recover from.
example_lines: He hit a haymaker in the second bar and it was over
Save the haymaker for the last line — make them feel it

definition: Directly responding to your opponent's specific lines in a battle — flipping their words back on them or disproving their claims. The best rebuttals turn an opponent's strength into a weakness.
origin: Legal/debate term brought into battle rap. Rebuttals show adaptability and quick thinking.
example_lines: His rebuttal was better than the original bar
You can't win a battle without a strong rebuttal

definition: A verse, round, or song so devastating that it metaphorically kills the opponent. If someone says you got put in a body bag, your career might be over. Used in battles and in describing lopsided features.
origin: Military/medical term for transporting the deceased. Applied to rap battles for complete, irreversible defeats.
example_lines: That feature put three rappers in body bags
He handed out body bags all night

definition: An affirmation meaning 'agreed,' 'understood,' or 'that works.' A one-word confirmation that became universal slang. Can close a deal, accept a challenge, or simply acknowledge what someone said.
origin: Emerged from Southern and New York slang in the early 2000s. Now used across hip-hop culture globally.
example_lines: Bet, I'll be there at 8
You dropping a tape? Bet.

definition: I understand — no more explanation needed. Used to cut short unnecessary back-and-forth when the message is already clear. Shows confidence and decisiveness.
origin: Emerged in trap culture as a way to communicate efficiency. The opposite of over-explaining.
example_lines: You need me to pull up? Say less.
Say less, I already know what it is

definition: Absolute truth — not just facts, but undeniable, unquestionable truth. Used to validate a statement so strong it needs no debate.
origin: Southern slang that spread nationwide through social media and rap culture in the 2010s.
example_lines: He's the hardest MC alive, big facts
Big facts — that album changed everything

definition: For real for real — extreme emphasis on sincerity. More serious than just 'for real.' Used to make clear that what you're saying is 100% genuine with no exaggeration.
origin: Text/social media abbreviation that entered spoken hip-hop vernacular in the 2010s.
example_lines: That was the hardest verse I've ever heard, frfr
I'm done playing games, frfr

definition: Immediately, off the top, or without thinking. Can mean something is obvious or it can describe rapping without preparation — straight from the mind with no written reference.
origin: Variation of 'off the top of the head.' Core to freestyle culture where rhyming unprepared is a mark of skill.
example_lines: Off top, that's the best verse on the album
He wrote that off top in five minutes

definition: My word is my oath — a sworn promise in hip-hop culture. More serious than a handshake, it means your reputation is on the line. Rooted in Five Percenter ideology where spoken word has binding power.
origin: Five Percent Nation teaching where the spoken word is a binding contract. Became foundational in New York hip-hop.
example_lines: Word is bond, I'll be there
He said word is bond and everybody knew he meant it

definition: Someone genuinely authentic — a person who keeps it real in all circumstances, doesn't switch up, and can be trusted completely. The highest form of character endorsement in street culture.
origin: Emerged from street culture as a way to distinguish genuine loyalty from performative allegiance.
example_lines: He's a real one — never switched up even when things got hard
Real ones are rare, hold onto them

definition: In a desperate, compromised, or embarrassing situation — financially broke, romantically rejected, or morally compromised. Can be self-aware or an insult.
origin: Spread through social media and hip-hop in the late 2010s to describe being in a pitiful state.
example_lines: He's down bad — begging online for money
Don't let them see you down bad

definition: Someone completely loyal — they'll ride with you through anything, good times and bad. A rider doesn't abandon you when it gets hard. Having a real rider is rarer than money.
origin: Street culture term rooted in the idea of riding with your crew through any situation.
example_lines: She's been a rider since day one
I need riders around me, not fans

definition: Trustworthy, reliable, and principled — someone who won't crack under pressure or sell you out. 'He's solid' is one of the highest endorsements in street culture.
origin: Street slang for someone with unshakeable integrity. Used to vet people before including them in serious matters.
example_lines: He's solid — never said a word even when they pressured him
Before you move with anybody, make sure they solid

definition: To arrive somewhere — often with an implied threat or challenge. 'Pull up' in a beef context means confrontation is coming. In a casual context it just means showing up.
origin: Driving slang — pulling a car up to a location. Evolved to mean arriving with intent.
example_lines: Pull up to the session if you want smoke
He pulled up and the whole energy shifted

definition: To leave quickly and without fanfare. Dipping is exiting a situation — usually because something is about to go wrong or because you're simply done.
origin: Street slang for a quick exit. The speed of a 'dip' implies urgency or cool detachment.
example_lines: Once the opps showed up, everybody dipped
I'm about to dip — this ain't my scene

definition: Money — specifically reliable, earned income. 'Getting bread' means getting paid. Bread implies consistency, not just a one-time score.
origin: Old slang rooted in bread as a necessity of life. If you have bread, you're taken care of.
example_lines: He's been getting bread since he was 16
Secure the bread before anything else

definition: Money — particularly cash. 'Chasing paper' means single-minded focus on making money. Paper implies hustle and pursuit.
origin: Old American slang for currency. Central to hip-hop's money vernacular since the genre's beginning.
example_lines: He was chasing paper before anybody believed in him
Get your paper right before you worry about anything else

definition: The relentless pursuit of money and success through any means available. Hustle is a mentality, not just an action — it's showing up consistently when others won't. Deeply embedded in hip-hop's core values.
origin: Pool hall slang for deception that evolved into a broader celebration of street entrepreneurship in hip-hop.
example_lines: The hustle never stops
He came from nothing — all hustle, no help

definition: The sustained, unglamorous work of building something from nothing. While hustle has an element of cleverness, grind is pure relentless effort. You grind when nobody is watching.
origin: Physical labor metaphor adopted by hip-hop to describe the daily work of building a career or income.
example_lines: He was on the grind for years before anyone noticed
Trust the grind even when it doesn't feel like it's working

definition: In the process of rising — building reputation, money, or status from a low position. It's a state of momentum, not arrival. Being on the come up means the work is paying off but you're not done yet.
origin: Street slang for upward mobility — referencing someone who is ascending in status.
example_lines: He's on the come up — don't sleep on him
Everybody wants to be your friend once you're on the come up

definition: A crew, gang, or neighborhood affiliation. Your set is your identity in street culture — who you represent and who will represent you. Sets have colors, signs, and territories.
origin: Gang culture terminology. A set is a local chapter of a larger gang or an independent neighborhood crew.
example_lines: He repped his set from day one
What set you from?

definition: The street corner where business is conducted, where crews post up, and where neighborhood life happens. The corner is both a physical place and a symbol of street life.
origin: Urban geography. The corner is the intersection of commerce and community in impoverished neighborhoods.
example_lines: He grew up on the corner and knew every face
The corner was where everything started

definition: Product being sold on the street — drugs. When someone says they have work, they're in business. 'Moving work' means actively selling.
origin: Street euphemism for drugs as inventory. Treating illegal product as a business commodity.
example_lines: He always had work when nobody else could find it
Moving work is all he knew growing up

definition: A large quantity of drugs — moving weight means operating at a wholesale level, not hand-to-hand retail. Rappers use it to signal serious street status.
origin: Drug trade terminology for quantity. Moving weight means you're a supplier, not just a street-level dealer.
example_lines: He went from the corner to moving weight
Moving weight is a different level of risk

definition: The supplier — the person above the plug who has direct access to the source. Having a connect means you can get product before it's been marked up multiple times.
origin: Drug supply chain terminology. The connect is a coveted and closely guarded relationship.
example_lines: He had a direct connect so the prices were different
Everybody needs a connect eventually

definition: Wisdom, knowledge, and valuable information — not jewelry. When someone drops jewels, they're sharing insight that took years to acquire. Rooted in Five Percenter philosophy where knowledge is treated as precious.
origin: Five Percent Nation teaching. Knowledge and wisdom are called jewels because they are rare, valuable, and must be protected.
example_lines: He dropped jewels on that track — real knowledge
Listen carefully, he's dropping jewels right now

definition: Clever, smooth, and slightly shady — slick talk is charming but manipulative. A slick rapper finds clever ways to say insulting things without being direct. Slick can be a compliment or a warning.
origin: Old American slang for someone who uses cleverness rather than force to get what they want.
example_lines: That bar was slick — said everything without saying anything
Don't let the slick talk fool you

definition: Ruthlessly impressive — cold means excellent with an edge of heartlessness. A cold verse doesn't care about your feelings. Cold is reserved for things that are so good they shock you.
origin: Slang that conveys excellence through emotional detachment. If something is cold, it hits without warmth — pure precision.
example_lines: That bar was cold — I had to pause the song
He's been cold since the jump

definition: Unpolished, unfiltered, and authentic. Raw means nothing has been softened or commercialized. It can describe music, a person, or a situation. A raw rapper doesn't care about radio — they care about truth.
origin: Slang for unprocessed, natural, or uncensored. In hip-hop it signifies genuine street authenticity.
example_lines: His delivery is raw — no auto-tune, no tricks, just bars
That tape was too raw for a label

definition: Officially authenticated or approved — to be stamped by someone respected means your credibility is verified. Getting stamped by a legend opens doors that money can't buy.
origin: Bureaucratic approval metaphor. In hip-hop, a stamp from the right person is a seal of authenticity.
example_lines: He got stamped by veterans — now nobody can question him
You need to get stamped before you step into this lane

definition: An exclamation of crew solidarity — reinforcing loyalty and shared identity. Used to punctuate a statement or show that your entire crew agrees. Also used as a general affirmative response.
origin: Gang and crew culture verbal signal of collective identity. Spread through trap music in the 2010s.
example_lines: Gang gang, we all eating now
Dropped a new song — gang gang

definition: Onomatopoeia for the sound of a car speeding away — tires screeching. Used as an ad lib or interjection to signal fast money, quick exits, or high energy. Associated with trap music's car culture.
origin: Phonetic spelling of tire screech. Became a ubiquitous ad lib in trap music and street vernacular.
example_lines: Pulled up in the foreign, skrrt skrrt
Skrrt on the opps

definition: To overcharge someone or take an unfair cut. If someone is taxing you, they're taking advantage of their position in the supply chain or relationship. Can also mean making someone pay for disrespect.
origin: Financial term applied to street economics and interpersonal dynamics.
example_lines: He's taxing everybody on the block — prices are ridiculous
You disrespect me and I'm taxing you for it

definition: Conspicuously displaying wealth and status — expensive clothes, jewelry, cars, and lifestyle. Stunting is performative flexing; it's making sure people see what you have.
origin: Emerged from New Orleans bounce culture. Stunting = performing, showing off. Popularized nationally through Southern rap.
example_lines: He pulled up stunting — full outfit, chain, foreign car
Stunting on 'em is the only response

definition: To display wealth, talent, or power — showing off what you have earned. Flexing is both an art and a statement. In hip-hop, the flex is often the point of the record.
origin: Physical flexing of muscles as a show of strength. Applied to displaying any form of power or achievement.
example_lines: The whole song is just a flex and it's perfect
He flexed on everybody who doubted him

definition: Head-to-toe in the best clothes, jewelry, and accessories — the full drip activated. When you're dripped out, every element of the outfit is intentional and expensive.
origin: Extension of 'drip' — the fashion embodiment of being fully loaded with style.
example_lines: Walked in dripped out — everybody's head turned
Dripped out from the shoes to the chain

definition: Always prepared — the discipline of maintaining your skills, finances, and position so you never have to scramble. 'Stay ready so you don't have to get ready' is the full saying.
origin: Military and street preparedness philosophy embedded in hip-hop culture.
example_lines: Stay ready — opportunities don't come back
He stayed ready while everybody else was sleeping

definition: A rapper's writing ability — their pen game. A sharp pen produces elite bars. When someone says an artist has 'pen,' it's one of the highest compliments in rap.
origin: The actual pen used to write lyrics became a symbol of lyrical ability. Having pen means your writing is undeniable.
example_lines: The pen is unmatched — every bar is intentional
You can't question his pen

definition: Conflict, tension, or problems — unwanted interference between people or groups. If there's static between two crews, beef is either happening or building.
origin: Radio/communication interference metaphor. Static disrupts the signal — in street terms, it disrupts the peace.
example_lines: There's been static between those two blocks for years
He doesn't want any static, he just wants his money

definition: Conflict or beef — wanting smoke means you're looking for a fight or confrontation. Giving smoke means bringing the aggression. Can be physical or lyrical.
origin: Fire/combat metaphor. Where there's smoke there's fire — and where there's smoke in hip-hop, there's beef.
example_lines: He wants smoke with everybody right now
Pull up if you want smoke — we're right here

definition: To disappear without explanation — cutting off contact completely. Ghosting someone means they simply no longer exist in your world. Can describe a person leaving a relationship or a rapper going dark.
origin: Paranormal metaphor — ghosts are invisible and untouchable. Applied to social disappearance.
example_lines: He ghosted after the deal fell through — never heard from him again
Once the money was gone, they all ghosted

definition: Knowledge that has been tested by experience — deeper than facts alone. In hip-hop and Five Percenter philosophy, wisdom is the second step after knowledge: you must be able to apply what you know.
origin: Five Percent Nation teaching. Wisdom is 'the wise words, ways, and actions of the original man.' Embedded in hip-hop's philosophical tradition.
example_lines: He speaks with wisdom — everything he says has weight behind it
Knowledge plus experience equals wisdom

definition: Assessing the energy or mood of a person or room. A vibe check determines if the situation is right — safe, authentic, or worth being in. Failed vibe checks get people cut off.
origin: Social media slang from the late 2010s that entered mainstream hip-hop vocabulary.
example_lines: Vibe check before you bring anybody around the crew
He failed the vibe check the moment he walked in

definition: The unspoken force a person or place carries — positive or negative. Hip-hop is deeply attuned to energy: who you bring around you, what spaces you occupy, and what you attract.
origin: Spiritual and physical concept embedded in hip-hop's Five Percenter and street philosophy roots.
example_lines: His energy is different — the whole room shifted when he walked in
Protect your energy from people who drain it

definition: Conversation exclusively about making money — not small talk, not gossip, just business and finance. Bag talk means the discussion has purpose and potential.
origin: Extension of 'the bag' — securing money. If you're only on bag talk, you're focused and purposeful.
example_lines: I only do bag talk — don't call me for anything else
The meeting was straight bag talk from the jump
